title: The Sigil of the Weeping Wood
premise: Isandro Coldharbour carves bone charms that whisper with the voices of the dead, a small illegal magic he has hidden for ten years in the city of Vaelmoor. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Isandro learns she is the last vessel of the Weeping Wood, a sentient forest whose covenant with the mortal realm was broken by the very mages who outlawed magic. Hunted by the Pale Office and betrayed by his oldest friend, Isandro must carry the child through the dying wood to the Covenant Stone before the thirteenth moon turns, sacrificing the charms that hold the voice of his dead wife. In the end he reforges the covenant at the cost of his own hearing — the dead fall silent forever — but the wood lives, the child speaks her first word in his language, and Isandro learns that survival without truth was never living at all.
about_author: Jonah Halloran is a former mortuary engraver from the northern coast who turned to fantasy after years of carving names into stone. He writes about grief, craft, and the stubborn persistence of old things in new worlds.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Door
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. In rain-soaked Vaelmoor, Isandro sells a widow a bone charm that carries her husband's last words, breaking the Edict of Silence one small crime at a time. The chapter establishes his loneliness, his guilt over ten years of hiding, and ends when a knock comes at midnight: a mud-caked child standing alone in the dark. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The child cannot speak but hums sounds that make Isandro's carved bones resonate on their own. When he touches her hand, he hears not the human dead but something vast and vegetal — a forest's memory. The Pale Office's whistles sound in the street below. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as Isandro realizes what he's harboring.

chapters.title: The Edict of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, with a flashback interlude. We learn how magic was outlawed thirteen years ago after the Sundering of the Weeping Wood, and how Isandro's wife Maren died in the purges. His friend Aldric Vane, now a Pale Office interrogator, arrives asking careful questions. Beat: loyalty strained by history; Isandro lies to a friend's face for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: POV Sefa (the child), rendered in strange, sensory prose. She remembers being a grove, then being a girl, and does not understand which she is. She trusts Isandro because his bones 'sing honest.' Through her eyes we see the city as a wound. Beat: identity theme established — she is neither tree nor child, and it terrifies her.

chapters.title: The Pale Office Calls
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Summoned formally, Isandro endures an interrogation by Aldric, who clearly suspects him but covers out of old affection. Isandro sees the Office's trophy wall: petrified branches of the Weeping Wood, still faintly weeping sap. Beat: claustrophobic tension; he realizes the Office knows the wood is regrowing somewhere.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. An old hedge-witch, Mother Quill, deciphers the child's humming: the covenant can only be reforged at the Covenant Stone before the thirteenth moon turns — six weeks. After that, the wood dies permanently and everything bound to it, including Sefa. Beat: the clock starts; resolve hardens into decision.

chapters.title: Leaving Vaelmoor
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro burns his charm stock, erasing ten years of the dead's voices including, painfully, all he has left of Maren except one hidden charm. He flees with Sefa through the sewer-gates as Aldric watches from a bridge and lets them go — or so it seems. Beat: grief and liberation braided together.

chapters.title: The Road of Gallows Trees
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The road north is lined with trees the Office hanged mages from; their corpses still whisper accusations. Sefa begins speaking single words of common tongue. They are ambushed by bounty hunters selling 'wood-touched' children. Beat: first violence; Isandro kills for the first time in ten years and is sickened by how easily it returns.

chapters.title: Aldric's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. Interrogating the captured bounty hunters, Aldric pieces together Isandro's route. Flashbacks reveal he and Isandro were apprentice friends, and that Aldric testified against Maren to save himself. He requests the hunt assignment personally — ostensibly to bring Isandro in alive. Beat: guilt weaponized; the antagonist becomes tragic.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Sheltering in a flooded chapel, Isandro uses his last Maren-charm to hear her voice one final time — and she tells him something he never knew: she died protecting the first seedling of the regrown wood. Sefa is that seedling's vessel. Beat: revelation reframes his grief; Maren chose this, and so must he.

chapters.title: Into the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. They cross into the wood itself — half-dead, gray, weeping black sap. The trees recognize Sefa and begin to wake, but the waking hurts her; she is burning herself out to feed them. Isandro realizes saving the wood may mean losing the girl. Beat: the central sacrifice made explicit; tenderness between the two deepens.

chapters.title: The Rootbound
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. They meet the Rootbound — survivors of the purges who merged themselves with the trees to escape, now half-feral guardians. Their leader, a woman with bark skin, tests Isandro by making him hear every dead soul he has ever sold a charm to. Beat: judgment scene; Isandro confesses his decade of cowardice aloud and is forgiven, barely.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. Aldric catches up alone, having quietly sabotaged his own squad. He begs Isandro to surrender, insisting the Office will spare the child if Isandro gives up the location of the Rootbound. Isandro refuses. They fight; Isandro wins but cannot kill him. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes — Aldric's loyalty to the Office is built on a lie he can no longer bear.

chapters.title: The Turning Moon
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Twelfth moon rises. The Office, tipped off by a surviving hunter, marches on the wood with fire-pots and iron. The Rootbound prepare a defense they cannot win. Sefa's hair has gone white and leaves grow in her wounds. Beat: dread and defiance; the community binds itself to a doomed stand.

chapters.title: Fire in the Gray Canopy
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The battle. The waking trees fight back, but fire spreads faster than roots. Mother Quill, arrived from the city, dies holding a gate open. Sefa pours too much of herself into the trees to save the wounded and collapses. Beat: cost of war; hope gutted at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Silent Carver
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Sefa lies dying because the covenant needs a full vessel at the Stone — a life willingly given. Isandro understands at last why Maren hid the seedling: someone had to choose. He carries Sefa toward the Covenant Stone through burning paths while the dead in his remaining charms scream warnings. Beat: desperate pilgrimage; love as fuel.

chapters.title: Aldric's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. Ordered to burn the Stone itself, Aldric stands before it and finally refuses. He turns his squad's orders back on them, buying Isandro minutes with his career and likely his life. Beat: redemption earned, not given; Aldric chooses truth over the institution that owns him.

chapters.title: The Covenant Stone
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the Stone, the covenant demands a price: a voice that hears the dead, freely silenced. Isandro offers his gift — the thing that defined him, his livelihood, his link to Maren. He presses the last charm to Sefa's chest and speaks the old words the child taught him. Beat: climax; the sacrifice is total and irreversible.

chapters.title: Green Returning
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Color floods the wood. Sefa wakes fully human — fully herself, whatever that means — and the trees live independent of her now. The surviving Office soldiers kneel or flee. Aldric, burned and broken, watches the canopy turn green and weeps. Beat: catharsis; rebirth witnessed by the penitent.

chapters.title: The Quiet After
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The silence where the dead used to be is enormous. Isandro grieves Maren a second time — truly this time, without her voice as a crutch. Sefa takes his hand and says her first full sentence: 'You don't need them to hear me.' Beat: mourning and grace; the theme lands — survival's price paid, truth chosen.

chapters.title: Edicts and Ashes
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, months later. In Vaelmoor, the Edict collapses as the wood's regrowth becomes undeniable; Aldric testifies about the Sundering's true cause, ruining himself and freeing others. Magic is not legal again, but it is no longer hunted. Isandro returns to carving — plain bone, no magic, honest work. Beat: the world shifts realistically, not utopian.

chapters.title: The First Green Year
chapters.summary: POV alternating Isandro/Sefa, closing epilogue-style. One year on, Isandro and Sefa live at the wood's edge teaching its language to settlers who ask permission instead of taking. On the anniversary night, the whole forest exhales — a sound only the once-hearer could have known, and somehow, faintly, he does. Final beat: identity remade; some prices buy more than they cost.
